summary: Revision 43 controller invariant is preserved as the normal acceptance destination while its transitional interpretation and controller-first build order are revised
body: OWNER CLARIFICATION, 2026-10-21. Preserve revision 43 as the destination invariant for the normal accepted pipeline: every model role ultimately executes through a registered CIS-owned role-specific controller, no model self-accepts, and CIS authority alone governs acceptance and promotion. Adapt its transitional interpretation: while contained routes are incomplete, explicitly authorized raw Claude Code, OpenRouter/Qwen, or Codex research may investigate architecture and produce clearly labeled advisory evidence. Such calls are not governed acceptance, promotion evidence, or proof that the final route exists. Supersede revision 43's controller-first build consequence as an unconditional execution sequence. Workbench and Brain are the spearhead of CIS. Work queue 4.37 proceeds top-down from human conversation through Brain deliberation, obstacle handling, governance rejection/correction and Card Factory, then downward through the pipeline. Detour into Claude, Hermes, Qwen, or other downstream controller construction only when dependency analysis demonstrates it blocks the next Brain/Workbench milestone. Provisional token, cost, or routing rules that are not real enforcement boundaries must not be treated as immutable architecture. The mission remains construction of the controlled environment.

summary: Queue 4.37 proceeds with a reversible Codex app-server Brain and Workbench experiment under explicit CIS containment and correction contracts
body: OWNER-AUTHORIZED DIRECTION. Treat Codex app-server as the candidate integration adapter for the Brain role using the owner's ChatGPT subscription. It is not the implementation-worker adapter and does not replace Hermes, Claude/Menter, Qwen/OpenRouter, the deterministic verifier, or CIS authority. Permanent architecture judgments: add a narrow DELIBERATE boundary upstream of Card Factory rather than weakening the worker ALLOW gateway; CIS remains authority and app-server thread/goal/approval state is evidence only; keep generic contracts provider-neutral; make cost_micros optional and provider-specific while retaining real wall-time and token/usage controls; require structured Brain obstacle reporting that distinguishes robust repair, justified temporary workaround, and human escalation; governance rejection must state the defect and required correction, and correction/resubmission must remain visible in Workbench; normalize app-server events into provider-neutral Workbench activity. The first slice is reversible and top-down: one pinned stdio app-server, one Brain deliberation thread, experimental API disabled, a protocol method allowlist, hosted web search disabled for the contained Brain, no direct implementation or repository-write route, structured output, one forced rejection/correction cycle, one forced process-failure recovery test, and observation of shared subscription quota. The idea of a separate guidance agent or skill is not a new queue item now; its desired behavior is folded into the Brain deliberation and governance contract until evidence shows a distinct component is needed.

summary: The app-server Brain direction is promising but cannot be called governed until containment, recovery, quota, and Workbench behavior are proven
body: OPEN PROOF OBLIGATION. The advisory Claude and Qwen reviews found no fatal architecture conflict, but they do not constitute CIS acceptance. Current primary documentation describes app-server as experimental and unsupported for production workloads. Hosted web_search is outside command-sandbox network controls; thread/shellCommand and experimental process/spawn can execute outside the ordinary sandbox; thread/inject_items can alter model-visible history outside a normal user turn; app-server goal budget limits are cooperative steering rather than an external hard stop; WebSocket is unsuitable; subscription authentication and quota are account-level failure and contention points; and MCP startup or mid-session failures can block or crash operation. Closure requires a pinned stdio-only Brain adapter with an explicit method allowlist, experimentalApi disabled, contained tool policy, external wall-time and token enforcement, structured output and correction/resubmission, normalized Workbench events, authentication/usage-limit failure states, process-crash recovery without blind resume, and evidence that no downstream controller work is pulled forward unless it is a demonstrated dependency. Until that proof exists, app-server output is advisory and the Brain route is not an accepted governed pipeline route.
